title: 八 · eight; the luckiest number and the eight trigrams
desc: Eight is the most coveted number in modern China through its near-homophony with 发 fā (to prosper), and the classical foundation of the eight trigrams that structure the Yijing.

title: 黑 · black, darkness, and the illicit
desc: Black on the surface, but the live sense is moral: the black market, the underworld, the hacker. The color that names everything that operates out of sight.

title: 很 · very; the empty intensifier
desc: 很 is the word for very, but its strangest job is doing nothing: Chinese needs a degree adverb before a plain adjective, and 很 fills that slot so quietly that 我很好 means simply I am fine, not I am very well.

title: 红 · red, the color of luck and celebration
desc: The cultural keystone color: weddings, New Year, the red envelope, and a century of revolutionary politics all run through this one character.

title: 九 · nine; the imperial number and the highest of the yang
desc: Nine is the largest single digit and the highest yang number, reserved for the emperor and the heavens: nine dragons, nine gates, the Nine-Five supreme position, the ninth heaven.

title: 两 · two (of); a pair; the tael, the other word for two
desc: 两 is the two used before measure words, the two of quantity and pairing, as opposed to 二 the two of counting and order, a distinction that is one of the first real puzzles a learner meets.

title: 零 · zero; raindrops, the fractional remainder, and the late invention of nothing
desc: Zero began as falling raindrops and the leftover odd remainder, taking on the meaning of mathematical nothing only late, the placeholder that Chinese numerals long managed without.

title: 六 · six; the six directions; a smooth and lucky number
desc: Six closes space into the six directions (the four compass points plus up and down) and, through its near-homophony with 流 liú (to flow), became a number for things going smoothly.

title: 念 · to recite, to keep in mind, to miss
desc: 念 holds the present moment 今 over the heart 心: to keep something in mind, to recite aloud, to long for what is absent. The 念 of 念佛 recitation, 想念 longing, and the single thought-moment of Buddhist psychology.

title: 七 · seven; the rhythm of mourning, festival, and the soul
desc: Seven measures the cycles of death and renewal in Chinese culture: the seven-day periods of mourning, the seventh-night lovers' festival, and the seven emotions of the heart.

title: 千 · thousand; a vast, uncountable many
desc: Thousand is the order of magnitude where a precise count gives way to poetic vastness: a thousand miles, a thousand autumns, ten thousand changes, the number that means simply too many to count.

title: 四 · four; the four directions; the homophone of death
desc: Four organizes the Chinese world into quarters, the four directions, four seas, four seasons, yet its near-homophony with 死 sǐ (death) makes it the most avoided number in modern China.

title: 它 · it; the non-human third person
desc: 它 began as a picture of a snake and once meant other; in the twentieth century it was reassigned to the non-human third person, completing the homophonous 他/她/它 triad that exists only in writing.

title: 完 · to finish; to be whole
desc: 完 means both whole and finished, and the bridge between them is intact completeness; its most important job is as a result complement, the 完 that ends 吃完, 做完, and 看完.

title: 五 · five; the organizing number of correlative cosmology
desc: Five is the center plus the four directions, the number that completes the Chinese cosmos: five phases, five colors, five tones, five flavors, five viscera, all keyed to one master grid.

title: 雪 · snow, whiteness, and vengeance
desc: Rain over a sweeping hand: snow is the precipitation you can hold. The same character means dazzling white and, by a buried metaphor, to wipe clean an old grievance.

title: 阴 · the shaded slope, the lunar, the covert
desc: The shadow half of the cosmos and the everyday word for an overcast day. From the dark side of a hill grew the lunar calendar, the hidden plot, and time itself as light and shade.

title: 最 · most; the superlative marker
desc: 最 is the single word that pushes any adjective to its limit: the -est of English, the most of comparison, the marker that turns 好 into 最好 and 后 into 最后.

title: 做 · to do, to make, to act as
desc: 做 is the everyday verb for doing and making, a late character built to carry the work that 作 had grown too literary to do, and the two still split the labor between them.

title: 曹操 · The Warlord-Poet
desc: The man who held the dying Han together by force, wrote some of the finest poetry in the language, and became Chinese literature's most magnificent villain.
